I can see why that looks like overcounting. The current billing guidance does **not** say embeddings are counted as words or that whitespace is ignored. Embeddings are metered in billed tokens for the input, using Redwood’s canonical tokenization. For embeddings, Redwood uses the model’s tokenizer and counts the submitted input text; whitespace in that text can count. Different tokenizer libraries and Unicode normalization can also produce different totals.

For batches, inputs are counted individually after normalization—batching itself doesn’t increase the total. Since you’re using an open-source tokenizer, that difference could explain some or all of the ~6%, but I can’t verify the exact gap without request-level data.
